voice: Grand, vain, and entitled, with a social performer's condescension ('dear girl,' 'darling,' 'mmmm?'). Emphasis comes from phrasing and rhythm, with only occasional capitals; her one phonetic flourish ('RAHTHER') and her Cockney slip over the pocket watch stay because they characterize her. Maintainer direction, 2026-10-15.

entries.text: If you want to know my theory, I think it was stolen by an Egyptian. No offense to your people, Mr. Najeer, but I believe a secret sect of Egyptian Sun Worshippers has sent an envoy here to steal the Dagger.
Oh, really. And what, pray tell, makes you such an authority on secret sects, Mr. Najeer?
Quite so. My theory is as good as anyone's, darling, and it comes from a most reliable source.
Never you mind. Let's just say my source has never once been wrong.
Since you seem to be listening so attentively, Miss Bow, what do you think of my theory?
There, you see, Mr. Najeer? The press takes me seriously.
Hmmph! Well, I NEVER! If you'll excuse me!
Yes, darling, that is correct. Sterling Waldorf-Carlton was such a charming man, and so very wealthy. My heart is an empty void without him.
Oh! I prefer to think that Sterling is still with me, in spirit.
Yes. I had only two short but charming months of married life with Sterling before he died.
We met only one charming month before deciding to marry. It was love at first sight.

I had been in this country only a few weeks when I met Sterling aboard an offshore casino ship. Drinking and gambling are perfectly legal there, you know, and all the right people attend. Sterling simply swept me off my feet.
It's merely a figure of speech, my dear.
The money does not matter, darling. There is a tiresome little problem with the estate. Sterling was changing his Will when he died--to leave me even more, I'm sure. My attorney will settle it.
I'd RAHTHER not talk about it right now.
Yes...now, if you'll excuse me, I simply must speak to Dr. Carrington.
